summary: Pinned model sessions divert to legacy variant during multi-wave canary glide-path
description: Issue summary: During a scheduled multi-wave canary for rw-bert-compat-v2.1 in a dedicated customer pool, a subset of long-lived user sessions that were explicitly pinned to the new variant were observed returning responses from the legacy v1.9 variant. Impact: NimbleDocs reported mixed inference outputs for ongoing conversational sessions affecting ~0.7% of requests for a small cohort; customer-facing SLAs risk due to inconsistent outputs. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (g2 instances), prod - us-west-2, canary rollout using staggered weight waves over orchestrator epoch windows. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start multi-wave canary (wave sizes 5% -> 20% -> 50%). 2) Create long-running streaming sessions with explicit model pin header. 3) Trigger a controlled edge-reshard (simulates a regional ingress rebalance) during the second wave. 4) Observe that ~1 in 150 sessions receive responses from rw-bert-compat-v1.9. Observed behavior: Pinned sessions lose variant affinity after the edge-reshard; traffic is transparently routed to legacy variant via fallback path rather than honoring explicit pin. Expected behavior: Sessions that are pinned should remain bound to the chosen variant for the session duration or follow explicit pin retention TTL; fallbacks should only apply when the pinned variant is unhealthy or unavailable. Interim mitigation: Support recommended immediate rollback of canary weight to previous stable wave and issued targeted prewarm for the pinned variant on affected pool. SRE applied emergency routing adjustment to prefer explicit pin claims over health-fallback for the cohort while investigation continues.
steps_to_reproduce: Initiate multi-wave canary deployment for rw-bert-compat-v2.1 in dedicated pool (5% -> 20% -> 50%).
Open long-lived streaming sessions and set X-Model-Pin header to v2.1 for test tenants.
Trigger an edge-reshard (move ~10% of ingress connections between edge nodes) during the second wave.
Send continued streaming requests on pinned sessions and observe returned variant metadata and outputs.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Edge epoch applied control-plane snapshot out-of-order relative to orchestrator leading to transient pin-map desynchronization.
Hypothesis B: Prewarm eviction heuristics suppressed v2.1 health score during the reshard window, causing fallback policy to prefer legacy variant despite pin token present.
Observed: traffic correlation shows rebind events align exactly with edge-reshard TTLs and snapshot timestamps; KV cache reconciliation lag ~250-400ms on affected nodes.
Reproduction: Localized test with simulated reshard reproduced mismatch when orchestrator snapshot commit-order is non-monotonic and prewarm probe backlog > 50ms.
resolution: In Progress - temporary mitigation applied (routing override to honor explicit model pins). Next steps: (1) backport snapshot ordering fix to orchestrator (PR linked), (2) adjust prewarm health suppression timeout to avoid short-window fallback during reshard, (3) add a canary gate that stalls weight advancement if any edge node reports epoch skew >100ms. Planned ETA for code fix: 2026-03-18; hotfix rollout to staging today. Postmortem to be posted to Confluence after resolution.
follow_up_actions: Backport and deploy orchestrator snapshot monotonicity fix (PR 7281) to prod-candidate cluster.
Lower prewarm health suppression debounce from 5s to 1s for dedicated pools with active pins.
Create a monitoring alert for edge/orchestrator epoch skew > 50ms and set an automated canary-hold action.
Schedule a postmortem with customer and internal teams; update canary runbook with edge-reshard guidance.
